body.statement:
A law and APE generated by some \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\) are equivalent to eight nonnegative measures \((
u_s)_{s\in S}\) with \(\sum_s
u_s\) a probability measure and \[P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}\int p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)d
u_{(x,r)}(u),\qquad \Delta=\sum_{s\in S}\int rac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}d
u_s(u).\] Conversely, every such family reconstructs one legal base law by \(\mu=\sum_s
u_s\), initial probabilities by Radon--Nikodym derivatives of \(\sum_r
u_{(x,r)}\) with respect to \(\mu\), and feedback probabilities by the corresponding response-coordinate marginals.
body.justification: This equivalence is the legal-kernel reconstruction step that prevents incompatible history-specific mixing laws.
body.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham use history densities satisfying pointwise compatibility; they do not replace them by eight jointly reconstructible response measures.
body.consumer: It turns the continuous-feedback identification problem into eight independent univariate moment problems without changing the model class.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\mu_x=\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}\).  First suppose that
\((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\), and define \(\nu\) as in
\(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}response\text{-}measures}\).  Nonnegativity follows from
\(\mathrm{ass{:}initial\text{-}kernel}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}feedback\text{-}kernel}\).  Moreover,
\[
 \sum_{x\in B}\sum_{r_0,r_1\in B}d\nu_{(x,r_0,r_1)}
 =\sum_{x\in B}h_x
   \left(\sum_{r_0\in B}g_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)\right)
   \left(\sum_{r_1\in B}g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)\right)d\mu
 =d\mu.
\]
Thus \(\sum_s\nu_s\) is a probability measure by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}base\text{-}law}\).  For a fixed \((x,y,z,w)\), summing over
the unused response coordinate gives
\[
 \sum_{r:r_y=z}d\nu_{(x,r)}
 =h_x g_{xy}(z,\cdot)
   \sum_{r_{1-y}\in B}g_{x,1-y}(r_{1-y},\cdot)d\mu
 =h_xg_{xy}(z,\cdot)d\mu.
\]
Multiplication by the two response probabilities from
\(\mathrm{ass{:}logit\text{-}response}\), followed by integration, gives the
displayed cell equation.  Summing the APE integrand against \(\nu_s\) instead
gives
\[
 \sum_s\int\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}d\nu_s
 =\int\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}d\mu=\Delta.
\]

Conversely, suppose that the eight finite nonnegative measures satisfy the
stated equations and that \(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\) is a probability measure.  For
\(x,y,z\in B\), define
\[
 \mu_x=\sum_r\nu_{(x,r)},\qquad
 \lambda_{xyz}=\sum_{r:r_y=z}\nu_{(x,r)}.
\]
Then \(\mu_x\ll\mu\), \(\lambda_{xyz}\ll\mu\), and
\(\lambda_{xy0}+\lambda_{xy1}=\mu_x\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}radon\text{-}nikodym\text{-}finite\text{-}family}\), choose
simultaneously measurable derivatives
\[
 h_x=\frac{d\mu_x}{d\mu},\qquad
 k_{xyz}=\frac{d\lambda_{xyz}}{d\mu},
\]
so that \(h_x\ge0\), \(\sum_xh_x=1\), \(k_{xyz}\ge0\), and
\(k_{xy0}+k_{xy1}=h_x\), all \(\mu\)-almost everywhere.  Set
\[
 g_{xy}(z,u)=
 \begin{cases}
 k_{xyz}(u)/h_x(u),&h_x(u)>0,\\
 1/2,&h_x(u)=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Division is used only on \(\{h_x>0\}\).  The resulting functions are
measurable Markov kernels, satisfy
\(h_xg_{xy}(z,\cdot)d\mu=d\lambda_{xyz}\), and obey all four weak-model
assumptions.  Sequentially drawing \(X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2\) from \(h,p,g,p\)
therefore gives
\[
 \int h_xp_x(y,\cdot)g_{xy}(z,\cdot)p_z(w,\cdot)d\mu
 =\int p_x(y,\cdot)p_z(w,\cdot)d\lambda_{xyz}
 =P(x,y,z,w).
\]
The same summation already proved the APE equality.  This proves both
directions without positing any cross-world independence: the product in the
forward direction is merely a coupling used to construct the response type.
